Soaring Financing Costs Threaten Commercial Real-Estate Deals
 
Plus, senior housing’s comeback is under way with billion dollar deal
 
By Craig Karmin
 

This is an edition of the Real Estate newsletter, a weekly briefing of the biggest commercial deals, news, analysis and trends in office, multifamily, retail and other commercial sectors. If you’re not subscribed, sign up here.

 

In commercial real estate, a lot can happen in six to 12 months. That’s the time it frequently takes between when a buyer signs a contract and when the sale is completed. With interest rates suddenly soaring, that’s more than enough time for financing costs to rise—sometimes by a lot. As Peter Grant reports, a growing number of commercial property buyers are threatening to walk away from recent transactions unless the seller offers better terms. “Rates went up, what, just a few days ago and I’m already getting calls where they’re talking retrade,” said Jeff Powers at Cushman & Wakefield.

 

Investment group BDT & MSD Partners is acquiring a high-end senior housing operator in a billion dollar deal, the latest sign that property investors are betting big on a senior housing comeback. BDT & MSD is taking a majority stake in Sunrise Senior Living, the fifth largest senior housing operator in North America and one of the largest such transactions in recent years. Peter has the scoop and explains why senior housing catering to well-off retirees is doing especially well.

 
 
 

The Surge in Rates Is Blowing Up Commercial Real-Estate Deals

 
 
SPENCER PLATT/GETTY IMAGES
 

A growing number of commercial real-estate buyers are threatening to walk away from recent transactions unless the seller offers better terms.

 

Rapidly rising interest rates are to blame.

 
 
 
$5 trillion
 

The total value of commercial and multifamily real-estate mortgages that are outstanding. That is far more than Americans owe on credit cards or auto loans combined.

Luxury Senior-Housing Company Locks In a $1 Billion Buyer

 
 
SUNRISE SENIOR LIVING
 

An investment group is acquiring a luxury senior-housing operator in a $1 billion deal, seeking to capitalize on the buying power of the aging baby-boom generation.

 
 
 

Data Points

 

• 73%: The increase in data-center construction spending over the past 12 months as of August, according to the Associated Builders and Contractors trade group, which analyzed Commerce Department data. The sector’s momentum defies the increase in material, labor and borrowing costs that have slowed other types of construction.

 

• 14.4%: The decline in retail employment in New York City last year compared with 2019, according to a report by the New York State Comptroller. Manhattan is missing the most jobs out of the five boroughs due to the postpandemic fall in tourism and office traffic, with employment levels there 21.2% below 2019 numbers.

 

• $45.9: Total profits, in billions, among Wall Street firms through the first half of 2026, according to the New York State Comptroller. That’s a 51.3% increase from the same period last year and bodes well for the city’s luxury residential market, since bankers and other financial professionals often use their bonuses for down payments.
